content.text:
No, Warp Terminal doesn't have an npm installer — it's a native app, not a Node.js package.

The standard ways to install it on macOS are:

- **Homebrew** (most common for dotfiles/scripted setups): `brew install --cask warp`
- **Direct download**: from warp.dev

If you're looking to automate it in your dotfiles, the Homebrew cask is the right approach.

- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

1	# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
2	# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
3	# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
4	# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
5	#
6	# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
7	# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
8	# TypeScript-only rule.
9	#
10	# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
11	# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
12	# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
13	# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
14	# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.
15	
16	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	# LANGUAGE & TONE
18	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	language: "en-US"
20	
21	reviews:
22	  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
23	  high_level_summary: true
24	
25	  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
26	  poem: false
27	
28	  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
29	  collapse_walkthrough: false
30	
31	  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
32	  request_changes_workflow: true
33	
34	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
36	  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
37	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	  profile: "assertive"
39	
40	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
42	  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
43	  # Different review instructions per file path.
44	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
45	  path_instructions:
46	    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
47	    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
48	    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
49	    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
50	    - path: "overrides/**"
51	      instructions: |
52	        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
53	        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
54	        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
55	        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.
56	
57	        For every PR, check:
58	
59	        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
60	           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.
61	
62	        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
63	           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
64	           complete page breakdowns.
65	
66	        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
67	           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
68	           cause stale data that persists until page reload.
69	
70	        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
71	           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
72	           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.
73	
74	        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
75	           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
76	           6 regions.
77	
78	        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
79	           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
80	           Use useMultiSite() for site context.
81	
82	        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
83	           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
84	           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
85	           personalisation data.
86	
87	        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
88	           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
89	           drawers.
90	
91	        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
92	           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
93	           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.
94	
95	        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
96	            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.
97	
98	        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
99	            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
100	            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.
101	
102	        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
103	            type(scope): description
104	            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
105	            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
106	            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
107	            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
108	            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.

111	    - path: "overrides/app/theme/foundation/**"
112	      instructions: |
113	        TIER 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM FROZEN FILE.
114	        This file contains Zimmermann brand design tokens. Treat every change with maximum scrutiny.
115	
116	        Check for:
117	        - Any colour value changes — flag the old and new hex values explicitly
118	        - Any font size, weight, or family changes — flag what changed
119	        - Any spacing scale changes — note which scale values were modified
120	        - Any breakpoint value changes — these affect every responsive component
121	        - Whether the change is additive (new token) or destructive (modifying existing token)
122	
123	        Destructive changes to existing tokens will affect every component in the design system.
124	        Always flag: "This change modifies an existing design token. Confirm with UI Designer that
125	        all consumers have been audited."

127	    # ── Tier 1: Shared critical hooks ───────────────────────
128	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts"
129	      instructions: |
130	        TIER 1 — HIGHEST RISK HOOK. useCurrentBasket is consumed by cart, checkout,
131	        order summary, promo code, and bonus product components simultaneously.
132	
133	        Every change requires:
134	        - Explicit audit of all import consumers: grep -r "use-current-basket" overrides/
135	        - Confirmation that the return shape has not changed
136	        - Confirmation that guest basket and registered basket merge behaviour is unaffected
137	        - A note in the PR description listing every consumer that was tested
138	
139	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts"
140	      instructions: |
141	        TIER 1 — useCurrentCustomer is the auth state source of truth.
142	        Any change affects login, registration, guest flow, and account pages simultaneously.
143	
144	        Check for:
145	        - Changes to customerType or isGuest return values
146	        - Changes to token handling or SLAS auth flow
147	        - Any new side effects on mount or unmount
148	
149	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts"
150	      instructions: |
151	        TIER 1 — useNavigation is consumed by header, footer, drawer menu, and breadcrumbs.

153	
154	        Check for:
155	        - Changes to locale-aware URL construction
156	        - Changes to the navigate() function signature
157	        - Any new required parameters
158	
159	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts"
160	      instructions: |
161	        TIER 1 — useMultiSite drives regional site, locale, and currency resolution.
162	        This affects all Zimmermann regional sites (AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK — 7–8 storefronts).
163	
164	        Check for:
165	        - Any hardcoded locale or currency values
166	        - Changes to site alias resolution logic
167	        - Whether changes have been tested against all configured locales, not just en-AU
168	
169	    # ── Tier 1: Runtime config ───────────────────────────────
170	    - path: "config/**"
171	      instructions: |
172	        TIER 1 — RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. These files control feature flags, API endpoints,
173	        and proxy routing for all environments.
174	
175	        Check for:
176	        - Any hardcoded API keys, secrets, or credentials — immediate block, must be in env vars
177	        - Any feature flag default that differs from the agreed rollout state
178	        - Any proxy host that differs between environment files — flag old vs. new value
179	        - Whether a change in default.js was intentionally not overridden in production.js

197	        - Any new secret references — confirm the secret exists in GitHub Secrets for all environments

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
#
# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
# TypeScript-only rule.
#
# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# LANGUAGE & TONE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
language: "en-US"

reviews:
  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
  high_level_summary: true

  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
  poem: false

  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
  collapse_walkthrough: false

  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
  request_changes_workflow: true

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  profile: "assertive"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
  # Different review instructions per file path.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  path_instructions:
    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
    - path: "overrides/**"
      instructions: |
        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.

        For every PR, check:

        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.

        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
           complete page breakdowns.

        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
           cause stale data that persists until page reload.

        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.

        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
           6 regions.

        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
           Use useMultiSite() for site context.

        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
           personalisation data.

        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
           drawers.

        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.

        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.

        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.

        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
            type(scope): description
            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.

    # ── Tier 1: Design tokens ───────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/theme/foundation/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM FROZEN FILE.
        This file contains Zimmermann brand design tokens. Treat every change with maximum scrutiny.

        Check for:
        - Any colour value changes — flag the old and new hex values explicitly
        - Any font size, weight, or family changes — flag what changed
        - Any spacing scale changes — note which scale values were modified
        - Any breakpoint value changes — these affect every responsive component
        - Whether the change is additive (new token) or destructive (modifying existing token)

        Destructive changes to existing tokens will affect every component in the design system.
        Always flag: "This change modifies an existing design token. Confirm with UI Designer that
        all consumers have been audited."

    # ── Tier 1: Shared critical hooks ───────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — HIGHEST RISK HOOK. useCurrentBasket is consumed by cart, checkout,
        order summary, promo code, and bonus product components simultaneously.

        Every change requires:
        - Explicit audit of all import consumers: grep -r "use-current-basket" overrides/
        - Confirmation that the return shape has not changed
        - Confirmation that guest basket and registered basket merge behaviour is unaffected
        - A note in the PR description listing every consumer that was tested

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useCurrentCustomer is the auth state source of truth.
        Any change affects login, registration, guest flow, and account pages simultaneously.

        Check for:
        - Changes to customerType or isGuest return values
        - Changes to token handling or SLAS auth flow
        - Any new side effects on mount or unmount

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useNavigation is consumed by header, footer, drawer menu, and breadcrumbs.
        A broken navigation hook breaks the global shell on every page.

        Check for:
        - Changes to locale-aware URL construction
        - Changes to the navigate() function signature
        - Any new required parameters

    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — useMultiSite drives regional site, locale, and currency resolution.
        This affects all Zimmermann regional sites (AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK — 7–8 storefronts).

        Check for:
        - Any hardcoded locale or currency values
        - Changes to site alias resolution logic
        - Whether changes have been tested against all configured locales, not just en-AU

    # ── Tier 1: Runtime config ───────────────────────────────
    - path: "config/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. These files control feature flags, API endpoints,
        and proxy routing for all environments.

        Check for:
        - Any hardcoded API keys, secrets, or credentials — immediate block, must be in env vars
        - Any feature flag default that differs from the agreed rollout state
        - Any proxy host that differs between environment files — flag old vs. new value
        - Whether a change in default.js was intentionally not overridden in production.js

    - path: "mobify.config.js"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — MRT DEPLOYMENT CONFIG. Changes here affect what gets deployed to
        Salesforce Managed Runtime. A bad change can break all SSR or CDN routing.

        Check for:
        - Any change to projectSlug — a mismatch causes silent deploy failures
        - Any change to ssrParameters.proxyConfigs — verify host values match B2C instances
        - Any change to ssrOnly or ssrShared path arrays

    - path: ".github/workflows/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — CI/CD PIPELINE. Changes here affect every developer's ability to ship.

        Check for:
        - Any removal of existing test gates (lint, unit tests, Lighthouse CI, bundle size)
        - Any new secret references — confirm the secret exists in GitHub Secrets for all environments
        - Any change to the deploy or activate steps — flag what changes and why
        - Whether the change maintains the feature → develop → main promotion flow

    # ── Tier 1: SSR server ──────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/ssr.js"
      instructions: |
        TIER 1 — SSR SERVER ENTRY. This file configures the Express server that runs on
        Salesforce Managed Runtime. A broken ssr.js takes down the entire storefront.

        Check for:
        - Any change to createApp() options — these affect all routes
        - Any new middleware that could affect response headers or caching
        - Any environment-specific logic that is missing an environment check
        - Whether the change has been tested with SSR enabled (not just client-side)

    # ── Tier 2: Global shell ─────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/components/header/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — GLOBAL HEADER. This renders on every page. Review as if this is production-critical.

        Check for:
        - Any change to the navigation data structure consumed from useNavigation
        - Any new prop added to a child component — confirm it's optional with a sensible default
        - Mobile/desktop breakpoint logic — confirm both viewports are covered
        - Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus management, aria labels on interactive elements
        - Any new external script or asset load — this adds to page weight on every route

    - path: "overrides/app/routes.tsx"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — ROUTE CONFIGURATION. Adding, removing, or reordering routes affects
        SEO, analytics, and every developer's feature work.

        Check for:
        - Any route removal — confirm a redirect exists before the route is dropped
        - Any path change — confirm SEO redirect mapping has been updated
        - Whether new routes use code splitting (@loadable/component)
        - Whether SSR is intentionally disabled on any new route (rare — flag if so)
        - Whether locale-prefixed path generation is still intact

    # ── Tier 2: Shared product components ───────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/components/product-tile/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — SHARED PRODUCT TILE. Used on PLP, search results, wishlists,
        recommendation carousels, and the homepage. Changes affect multiple pages.

        Check for:
        - Any change to required props — will break all consumers if made non-optional
        - Any new data dependency from a hook — confirm that hook is available in all
          contexts where product-tile is rendered (PLP, search, wishlist, recommendations)
        - Image lazy loading — confirm it's still applied
        - Wishlist toggle functionality — confirm it still works for both guest and registered users

    - path: "overrides/app/components/display-price/**"
      instructions: |
        TIER 2 — PRICE DISPLAY. Used across PDP, PLP, cart, and order history.
        Price display bugs are immediately visible to customers.

        Check for:
        - Correct handling of all price types: regular, sale/strikethrough, promotional, range
        - Currency formatting — confirm it uses the locale-aware formatter, not hardcoded symbols
        - Sale price display — confirm strikethrough logic is not broken

    # ── Checkout pages ───────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/pages/checkout/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD A — CHECKOUT. This is the highest-revenue-risk area of the codebase.

        Check for:
        - Any change to the basket mutation sequence — order of operations matters for SCAPI
        - Payment handling — confirm no payment data is logged or exposed in error messages
        - 3DS / async payment flow — confirm the PaymentProcessing intermediate page still works
        - BOPIS vs. standard delivery toggle — confirm switching modes doesn't corrupt shipment data
        - Guest vs. registered checkout state — confirm both flows still work after the change
        - Form validation — confirm required fields still prevent submission when empty

    # ── PDP / PLP ────────────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD B — PDP. The product detail page is the primary conversion entry point.

        Check for:
        - Variant selection logic — confirm all variation attributes still resolve correctly
        - Add to cart — confirm ATC still fires the Einstein sendAddToCart event
        - Image gallery — confirm mobile swipe and zoom still work after any changes
        - SSR data prefetch — confirm useProduct is still being prefetched server-side
        - Structured data — confirm schema.org Product markup is still present in the output

    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-list/**"
      instructions: |
        SQUAD B — PLP. Faceted search, refinements, and sorting are SEO-critical.

        Check for:
        - URL-based refinement state — confirm filters are reflected in the URL for SEO
        - Pagination — confirm URL-based pagination is intact (not scroll-based pagination)
        - Refinement removal — confirm the "clear all" and individual remove buttons still work
        - Page Designer slot — confirm the promotional banner slot still renders

    # ── QA feature files ─────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "e2e/features/**"
      instructions: |
        GHERKIN FEATURE FILES — source of truth for QA. Lead QA must validate before
        the paired Playwright spec is generated.

        Check for:
        - Jira traceability tag present: @SFCC-NNN
        - Area tag present: @checkout, @search, @account, @pdp, @plp, or @integrations
        - P0 journeys tagged @p0 — verify the scenario qualifies (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant)
        - No technical implementation detail in scenario steps — no selectors, URLs, or code references
        - At least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario per feature file
        - Background block used for shared preconditions, not repeated in each scenario
        - File under 150 lines — flag if exceeded, suggest splitting by scenario group
        - Baseline regression files (in regression/) are prefixed BASELINE- and use
          @baseline @regression tags (no Jira key tag)
        - DELTA comments present where SFCC behaviour is known to differ from Magento baseline

    # ── General hooks ────────────────────────────────────────
    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
      instructions: |
        HOOKS — Shared application logic. Check every hook change for:

        - Whether the return value shape has changed — even adding a key can cause
          consumer components to render differently if they spread the return value
        - Whether the hook adds a new required parameter — this is always a breaking change
        - Whether cleanup functions (useEffect return) are still present where needed
        - Whether the hook is safe to call during SSR (no window/document access without guards)
        - Whether React Query cache invalidation is correct after mutations

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # TOOLS — static analysis CodeRabbit runs automatically
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tools:
    eslint:
      enabled: true
    # Detect hardcoded secrets
    gitleaks:
      enabled: true
    # Project-specific pattern rules — a11y (JSX) and naming/structure checks.
    # Tested locally with the ast-grep CLI against fixtures + real files before landing.
    ast-grep:
      rule_dirs:
        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules"
      util_dirs:
        - ".coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/utils"
      essential_rules: true
    # npm/package-lock.json dependency vulnerability scanning (OSV.dev database)
    osvScanner:
      enabled: true
    # React-specific security/performance/correctness/accessibility scanner
    reactDoctor:
      enabled: true
    # Requires semgrep.yml in repo root (see that file) — payment-credential-logging
    # and unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML taint/pattern rules, tested locally.
    semgrep:
      enabled: true
      config_file: "semgrep.yml"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # AUTO-REVIEW triggers
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Review every push to a PR, not just on open

    # Don't waste review on draft PRs

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PRE-MERGE CHECKS — actual merge-blocking gates (requires
  # request_changes_workflow: true above to enforce `error` mode).

    # path-scoped, so it can't distinguish shared components/exported hooks
    # (which need JSDoc per components.md) from leaf components (which don't).
    # Replaced by the docstring-convention-compliance custom_check below.

      mode: "off"
    title:
      mode: error
      requirements: >-
        Must follow Conventional Commits format: type(scope): description.
        Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci,
        chore, upstream-sync. Scope is optional but encouraged.

      mode: error
    # Jira Forge app is not yet installed in the Atlassian instance — this has
    # nothing to assess against until that connection exists. Flip to `error`
    # once installed (see knowledge_base.jira below).
    issue_assessment:
      mode: warning
    custom_checks:
      - name: "Docstring convention compliance"
        mode: error
        instructions: >-
          Fail this check only if the PR adds or modifies (a) a component consumed
          by 2 or more callers (a shared component per protectedFiles.md/components.md),
          (b) an exported hook under overrides/app/hooks/**, or (c) a utility function
          with non-obvious behaviour — and the added/modified declaration does not
          have a JSDoc comment (hooks must include a @returns description).
          Do NOT fail for: leaf/single-consumer components, trivial or self-evident
          utilities, type-only files, test files, or story files. Pass if no
          qualifying declaration was added or modified in this PR.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # FINISHING TOUCHES — on-demand generation via PR checkbox or
  # @coderabbitai command
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    docstrings:
      enabled: true

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# KNOWLEDGE BASE — external context sources
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  jira:
    # NOTE: this only scopes context once the Jira Forge app is installed and
    # connected via the Atlassian Marketplace — it does not establish that
    # connection itself. As of this config, the Forge app is NOT yet installed
    # in zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net. Link a Jira issue by pasting its
    # URL into the PR description (no auto-detection from branch name).
    usage: enabled
    project_keys:
      - "SFCC"
  code_guidelines:
    # AGENTS.md is already covered by CodeRabbit's own default file patterns
    # (confirmed in docs) — listed explicitly anyway for visibility. The
    # .claude/rules/*.md files are NOT covered by any default pattern, and

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to | Allowed? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Primary working context for new work |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | ✅ Yes | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift |
| `develop` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
| `main` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.

If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.

## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced

Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:

- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a

- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" fontSize="14px" />

// ✅ token
<Box color="brand.primary" padding={4} fontSize="sm" />
```

**Not currently mechanically enforced.** Unlike the accessibility rules in
[components.md](./components.md), there's no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule watching for
a raw hex code or `px` value landing in a Chakra prop or `.scss` file yet — this is a strong
candidate for the same treatment (ast-grep can pattern-match a hex-colour or `px` literal
inside a JSX attribute value) if hardcoded values keep slipping through review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

## File naming and folder structure

- **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`,
  `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
- **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case
  filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`). This makes the origin of a
  file obvious at a glance.
- **Component folder layout:** each component lives in its own folder under
  [overrides/app/components/](../../overrides/app/components/). Use `index.tsx` for the
  component itself so imports stay clean:

  ```
  overrides/app/components/productTile/
    index.tsx              ← the component
    index.stories.tsx      ← Storybook story
    index.test.ts          ← Vitest (only if logic-heavy)
    types.ts               ← only if props/types are shared with sibling files
    productTile.scss       ← only if Chakra props are insufficient
  ```

  Import as `import ProductTile from '.../components/productTile'`.

---

## Utilities

- **Pure functions** — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment.
- **No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`** — utilities must not depend on hooks
  (it's the other direction).
- **Vitest required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports or
  one-liners don't need a test.

---

## Imports

- **No circular imports** — if file A imports from file B, B must not import from A
  (check one level deep).
- **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels** — flag for path-alias review.
- **No imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths** — use the
  package's published entrypoints (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`).
- **No imports from a later-sprint feature** — cross-check
  `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.

# Components, Hooks & Storybook Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this project. Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions for "I forgot to mark it optional." - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get these right at authoring time:** - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to announce. - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). --- ## Composition — writing a "clean" component Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline state belongs in a custom hook instead. - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new dependency needed). - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a one-line side effect. Keep it browsable — a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. ### When a story is required - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). # Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; all specs run on every feature PR against localhost).

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 7 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US — combining domestic and international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`

The project-level `Project Name_Peer Review Checklist.xlsx` (CODE REVIEW tab) is a generic Accenture PDC template with 31 items across 5 categories. The current checklist is **not applicable** to the Zimmermann PWA for three reasons:

|---|---|

|---|---|

|---|---|
